The residential grid is a compact run of front-gable houses, not the long antique-market sheds that sit farther up the highway. It is the community and school-district name for a stretch of southern Delaware County covering Concord Township, Chester Heights Borough, and Bethel Township. There is no Garnet Valley borough hall and no Garnet Valley line on a deed. People use the name anyway. Mail for a great many of these houses arrives through Glen Mills with ZIP 19342, which does not make the house part of a borough called Glen Mills either.

Two-story colonials, some larger homes with hips and a garage toward the street, vinyl walls, and architectural shingles rather than historic slate. Streets were laid out in pods. This is the Delaware County crossroads, not the Bucks County township that shares the Newtown name. The intersection itself is commercial: low roofs, parking, and the traffic of West Chester Pike and Newtown Street Road. The houses are on the wooded side streets, ZIP 19073, on lots larger than Aston's twins and less formal than the stone Main Line in Radnor.

Two generations share those streets. Mid-century colonials and split-levels have simpler gables, boxed soffits, and modest chimneys. Much newer houses are larger, with hip roofs, several valleys, dormers, and a garage gable facing the driveway. The canopy is real. Driveways are long. A single recent roof can carry more area than a short Media block would suggest, without any of Media's Victorian cutting.

Newtown Township is the municipality. Berwyn and Paoli sit nearby across the Chester County line, but an address here is still Delaware County ground. Exterior work splits by era. Neither era is slate by default, and neither one is a postwar ranch along PA 452.
